To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The elasticity of the extracellular matrix regulates differentiation of oligodendroglial progenitor cells in a non-muscle II-dependent manner, 2) Schwann cells differentiate normally in response to matrix stiffness, and 3) Schwann cell differentiation is potentiated by high levels of laminin on rigid matrices.

(1) ECM elasticity modulates the differentiation of oligodendroglia and Schwann cells in vitro; (2) the response of oligodendria to ECM elasticity depends on NMII; (3) the effect of matrix rigidity on Schwann cell differentiation is independent of NMII.

the role of the extracellular matrix in the development and regeneration of the peripheral nervous system.
the role of mechanotransduction in myelinating glia and the potential to harness this mechanism to promote myelin repair.
the development of biomaterials for the regeneration of the central and peripheral nervous system.
